questions.q: Why does every feature window filter orders to order_date <= SNAP (the snapshot date)?
options: It makes the groupby run faster
The snapshot date is the only date stored in the orders table
It removes duplicate customers
Rows dated after the snapshot describe the future the model is supposed to predict, so using them is leakage
questions.explain: The model must only see what was known on the snapshot. In this database 371 orders are dated after 30 June 2025, and they must not become features.

questions.q: The 'days since last order' rule flagged the top 10% of customers and reached a precision of 0.183. The break-even precision is 0.208. What does that mean?
options: Acting on the rule would be profitable
Acting on the rule would lose money under the illustrative costs, because fewer than break-even of contacted customers would have churned
The rule has perfect recall
The rule is better than logistic regression
questions.explain: Below the break-even precision, each contact costs more than it earns in expectation. This is why baselines are compared to the break-even, not just to each other.

questions.q: Why was the ambition target (cross-validated precision at the top 10% of at least 0.32) set only after the baselines were computed?
options: Baselines are needed to compute cross-validation
Scikit-learn requires a baseline before scoring
A target invented before you see the baselines is a guess; the best rule (0.268) gives it evidence
Targets can only be set on the test set
questions.explain: Lesson 3 deliberately left the ambition target open. Setting it relative to what a simple rule already achieves keeps it honest and meaningful.

questions.q: Why are median imputation, scaling, and encoding placed inside a Pipeline instead of applied to the whole table first?
options: So each cross-validation fold fits them on its own training rows only and no validation or test information leaks in
Pipelines are required by scikit-learn for logistic regression
It prevents missing values from ever occurring
It lets you skip the train/test split
questions.explain: Fitting a median or scaler on all rows lets held-out rows influence training values. Inside a pipeline, every fit uses training rows only.

questions.q: Why does this capstone use a stratified random split by customer instead of a time-aware split?
options: Random splits are always more accurate
Time-aware splits are not allowed in scikit-learn
The dataset has no dates
There is a single snapshot and one label window, so there is no earlier period with known outcomes to train on
questions.explain: A time-aware split needs several snapshots with observed outcomes. With one snapshot, a stratified split is the honest option, and the limitation should be stated.
